mostWorthwhile.text: Separating the copied chromosomes before dividing the cytoplasm made the distinction between those processes clear; the two-nucleus intermediate reinforced it.

leastWorthwhile.text: The failed actin-and-myosin attempt was frustrating: the cell already had separated chromosomes and an intact membrane, but the need to combine the two cutaway views first was not obvious.

surprise.text: Phospholipids and proteins first formed vesicles rather than adding directly to the cell; the following growth illustration explained their role.

arbitrary.text: Joining the enlarged cell body to the separated chromosome sets felt somewhat like assembling representations rather than performing a clearly described biological action, although it produced a useful two-nucleus intermediate.

continue.text: I would continue: the staged constructions clarified how a complete genome reaches each daughter, and the final mention of different gene-expression patterns suggests an interesting next connection. The picture descriptions are plans, so I cannot judge finished artwork or student comprehension.
